newsitem.title: USA: Shell Peru eyes export mkts for Camisea reserves.
newsitem.headline: Shell Peru eyes export mkts for Camisea reserves.

text.p: Shell Peru said Wednesday it will have 30,000 barrels a day extra of liquefied petroleum gas for export when gas from Peru's Camisea hydrocarbon fields begins to flow into Lima by 2002.

"No decision has yet been made on how best such an export volume could or should be structured and marketed, but there appears to be sufficient interest already in these volumes, primarily but not exclusively around the Pacific Rim," said Bernard Fogarty of Shell Peru, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell.

The Camisea reserves, situated 310 miles (500 kms) east of Lima, are still only in the beginning stages of development but have been estimated to hold 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids.

Shell, which is the operating partner of the Camisea project with Mobil, has said it hopes to produce gas as early as 1999 but full development of the project would not bring gas or LPG to the capital until 2002.

Fogarty said that even if Lima -- the largest LPG market in Peru -- were to experience a high growth rate in demand for liquids, total demand in 2002 would still be about half of the expected Camisea output.

A proposed fractionator is estimated to produce about 35,000 to 50,000 barrels per day of LPGs, of which 60 percent will be propane. Propane is a leading LPG used as chemical feedstock and a home heating and cooking fuel.
"Domestic demand is insufficient to take up the whole supply," said Fogarty, citing cheaper power costs possibly in the future due to Camisea as further eroding the LPG market.
Gas-fired generation of electricity that is supplied to smaller businesses and residential areas competes with LPGs.
